text: Philip Roth's Portnoy's Complaint was banned in Australia in 1969, when the government prevented its importation after the novel was deemed obscene. In September 1970 Dalton's voluntarily withdrew it from sale at its Garema Place bookstore after a police visit. Penguin Books was prosecuted after printing a local edition; it was convicted of breaching censorship laws in Victoria and fined $104.50, and Victoria Police seized 300 copies. The ban was lifted in June 1971.
